Rashi on Niddah 57b:11:1.english: An examination cloth - A cloth with which she examines [herself].

Rashi on Niddah 57b:11:2.hebrew: עגול - אין זה דם בדיקה, דדרך קינוח להיות משוך:
Rashi on Niddah 57b:11:2.english: Round - This is not examination blood, as the manner of wiping is to be elongated.

Rashi on Niddah 57b:12:1.hebrew: דארגישה - בשעת בדיקה. ועגול להכי טהור, לעולם דאימור הרגשת עד הואי, שציערתה בדיקת העד:
Rashi on Niddah 57b:12:1.english: That she sensed - At the time of the examination. And a round [stain] is pure for this reason: Actually, we say that it was the sensation of the examination cloth, for the examination with the cloth caused her pain.

Rashi on Niddah 57b:16:1.english: [If found] on her flesh, [and there is] uncertainty whether it is impure or pure, it is impure - All of it is explained below [in the Gemara].

Rashi on Niddah 57b:16:2.hebrew: ובמגעות ובהיסטות הלך אחר הרוב - אשה שלא מצאה כתם, והרי היא מחזקת עצמה בספק נדה, כגון שאין לה וסת ורגילה לראות תדיר, ונגעה או הסיטה, הלך אחר רוב ימיה: אם רוב ימיה רגילה לראות, מגעה והסיטה טמא, ואע"ג דהשתא לא ארגישה:
Rashi on Niddah 57b:16:2.english: And with regard to touching and with regard to moving, follow the majority - A woman who did not find a stain, and she holds herself in doubt of [being a] niddah, such as where she has no established period and is accustomed to see [blood] frequently, and she touched or moved [an object] — follow the majority of her days: If for the majority of her days she is accustomed to see [blood], her touch and her movement are ritually impure, and even though now she did not sense [a discharge].

Rashi on Niddah 57b:1:1.hebrew: הרואה כנגד בית התורפה - אותו מקום, דאיכא למימר דם מאותו מקום נפל להתם, וטמאה:
Rashi on Niddah 57b:1:1.english: A woman who sees opposite the pudenda - [That is,] that place [the private parts], as it can be said that blood fell from that place to there, and [therefore] she is ritually impure.

Rashi on Niddah 57b:1:2.english: On her heel or on the tip of her big toe, she is ritually impure - [This refers to] the tip of the big toe of the foot. And in the Gemara, it explains the reason.

Rashi on Niddah 57b:22:1.hebrew: דאזדקרה - זקפה עצמה לאחוריה. ואע"ג דעברה בשוק של טבחים – טמאה, דאי מעלמא אתאי, על חלוקה אבעי ליה לאשתכוחי:
Rashi on Niddah 57b:22:1.english: That she arched backward - She straightened herself backward. And even though she passed through the market of butchers, she is ritually impure; for if it had come from the outside world, it should have been found on her robe.

Rashi on Niddah 57b:2:1.hebrew: מבפנים - בין שני שוקים, כל גובהן מן הארץ:
Rashi on Niddah 57b:2:1.english: On the inner side - Between the two legs, along their entire height from the ground.

Rashi on Niddah 57b:2:2.english: On the outside - On this side and on that side [i.e., the outer sides of the legs].

Rashi on Niddah 57b:2:3.hebrew: צדדים - אחורי השוק כל גובהן כנגד העקב, ולפניו כל גובהן כנגד הרגל:
Rashi on Niddah 57b:2:3.english: The sides - The back of the leg along its entire height opposite the heel, and in front of it along its entire height opposite the foot.

Rashi on Niddah 57b:3:1.english: From the belt and below - It is opposite the pudenda.

Rashi on Niddah 57b:3:2.hebrew: אם מגיע כנגד בית התורפה - כגון שנמצא בראש בית ידה סמוך ליד, שפעמים שפושטתן מזרועה ונופל כנגד מטה:
Rashi on Niddah 57b:3:2.english: If it reaches opposite the pudenda - For example, where [the stain] was found at the end of her sleeve near the hand, for sometimes she slips them [the sleeves] off her arm and it falls downwards.

Rashi on Niddah 57b:3:3.english: Not opposite the genital area - For example, where [the stain] was found near her shoulder.

Rashi on Niddah 57b:4:1.english: Because it turns around - There are times when the top of the robe is inverted toward her lower front [i.e., her pudenda].

Rashi on Niddah 57b:4:2.english: And likewise with regard to a poleyos - A wrap with which she covers herself; orel in Old French.

Rashi on Niddah 57b:8:2.hebrew: עומדת טמאה - דאיידי דדחיק לה עלמא, דמעומד השתינה ולא יכלה לעצור, הדור מי רגלים למקור ואייתו דם:
Rashi on Niddah 57b:8:2.english: Standing, she is impure - Since she was pressed by the crowd, so that she urinated while standing and was unable to hold [it] in, the urine returned to the uterus and brought blood.

Rashi on Niddah 57b:8:3.hebrew: יושבת טהורה - דמכה יש לה במקום מי רגלים, שאין דרך דם נדה לצאת עם מי רגלים:
Rashi on Niddah 57b:8:3.english: [If she is] sitting, she is ritually pure - For she has a wound in the place of urine, as it is not the way for menstrual blood to emerge with urine.

Tosafot on Niddah 57b:15:1.hebrew: אימור הרגשת שמש הואי - וא"ת: אמאי לא נקט הרגשת מי רגלים כמו לעיל, ואע"פ שלא הטילה, כדאמר בריש מכילתין, והל"ל כסבור' הרגשת מי רגלים הוא? וי"ל: דהכא זמן מועט בין תשמיש למציאת הדם, והיתה יודעת אם תרגיש במי רגלים; אבל לעיל, בין פקידה לפקידה יש זמן ארוך, והרבה פעמים יש הרגשת מי רגלים בינתיים:
Tosafot on Niddah 57b:15:1.english: Say that it was the sensation of the [male] organ - And if you say: Why did [the Gemara] not state "the sensation of urine", as above, and even though she did not urinate, as [the Gemara] states at the beginning of our tractate, and it should have said: "[She was] thinking that it is the sensation of urine"? And one can say: Here, there is a short time between intercourse and the finding of the blood, and she would know if she felt [the sensation of] urine; but above, between examination and examination there is a long time, and many times there is a sensation of urine in the interim.

Tosafot on Niddah 57b:16:1.hebrew: ובמגעות ובהיסטות הלך אחר הרוב - פ"ה: אשה שאין לה וסת, ורגילה לראות תדיר, ובודקת עצמה תמיד, וכל זמן שלא בדקה עצמה מחזקת עצמה בטומאה; הלכך, אם רוב ימיה היא טמאין — טמאה. וזהו תימה, שזו החומרא לא מצינו בשום מקום! דהא אשה שיש לה וסת — דיה שעתה, וטומאה דמעת לעת אינה אלא באין לה וסת, ולא מפקידה לפקידה, ואפי' ברואה; וכ"ש הכא, דאין כאן אלא כתם, ואין לחלק בין ברואה תדיר בין שאינה רואה תדיר. ונראה, דקאי אנמצא על חלוקה (ספק טמא ספק טהור); וקאמר, דאם אחרי מציאת הכתם רוב ימיה טמאין — טמאה, ואף על גב דעברה בשוק של טבחים, ולא אמרינן: אי מגופה אתא, על בשרה איבעי ליה לאשתכוחי:
Tosafot on Niddah 57b:16:1.english: And with regard to touchings and shiftings, follow the majority - Rashi explained: [This refers to] a woman who does not have an established period, and is accustomed to see [blood] frequently, and examines herself constantly; and whenever she did not examine herself, she holds herself in a presumption of impurity. Therefore, if for the majority of her days she is impure, she is impure. And this is astonishing, for we do not find this stringency anywhere! For behold, [in the case of] a woman who has an established period, her time suffices [for her]; and the [retroactive] impurity of a twenty-four-hour period (me'et le'et) applies only to one who does not have an established period, and not from examination to examination, and [this is so] even when she [actually] sees [blood]! And all the more so here, where there is nothing here but a stain, and one cannot distinguish between one who sees [blood] frequently and one who does not see frequently. And it appears that [this clause] refers to [a stain] found on her robe (uncertain whether impure or pure); and it is saying that if, following the finding of the stain, the majority of her days are impure, she is impure, even though she passed through a marketplace of butchers, and we do not say: "If it came from her body, it should have been found on her flesh."

Tosafot on Niddah 57b:19:1.hebrew: אמר מר על בשרה כו' - ולבסוף פריך מינה לשמואל. והא דלא פריך מינה ברישא, אלא פריך ממגעות והיסטות דסיפא ברישא, משום דפשוט הוא יותר; אבל רישא, מיבעי ליה לתרוצי ברישא, והדר פריך מינה:
Tosafot on Niddah 57b:19:1.english: The Master said: "On her flesh," etc. - And ultimately it raises an objection from it against Shmuel. And as for the fact that it did not object from it at first, but rather objected from [the clause regarding] touching and moving in the latter clause first, [this is] because that is more straightforward; but the first clause, it needed to resolve first, and then it raises an objection from it.

Tosafot on Niddah 57b:1:1.hebrew: הרואה כתם - ת"ש: האשה שעושה צרכיה. תימה: מאי מהדר אפירכות? הא כמה משניות פ' בא סימן ודם הנדה בדיני כתמים, וליפרוך מינייהו; ולא שייך לשנויי עלייהו לא הרגשת עד ולא הרגשת שמש! ואומר הר"י, דמדיני כתמים ליכא למפרך, דהיינו יכולין להעמיד שיש זמן מרובה משעת הכבוס, ואימור הרגישה ולאו אדעתה. אבל בשמעתין, פריך מכתמים דבבשרה, דאין רגילות לשהות כתם בבשר בלא דעתה, שלא ייבש ויפול. מיהו, ברייתא דג' ספקות דמייתי לקמן, פריך מחלוקה, כמו שנפרש בההיא! וי"ל, דמשמע דזמן מועט היה שם, דומיא דבשר, ומשני דמזמן רחוק הוה, ואימור ארגשה ולא אדעתה; אי נמי, כיון דרוב ימיה טמאים, יש לחוש:
Tosafot on Niddah 57b:1:1.english: A woman who sees a stain - Come and hear: "A woman who is relieving herself [urinating]..." It is astonishing: Why does [the Gemara] seek out [difficult] objections? Behold, there are several mishnayot in chapter Ba Siman and [chapter] Dam HaNiddah concerning the laws of stains, so let it object from them! And it would not be applicable to answer regarding them neither the sensation of an examination cloth (ed) nor the sensation of the coital organ (shamash)! And the Ri says that from the laws of stains [on garments] there is no [valid] objection, for we would be able to establish [those mishnayot as referring to a case] where there is a long time from the time of laundering, and [one could] say: She sensed [an emission], but was not mindful of it (lav addatah). However, in our sugya, it objects from stains that are on her flesh, for it is not usual for a stain to remain on the flesh without her knowledge without drying up and falling off. However, the baraita of the three uncertainties that [the Gemara] cites below objects from [a stain found on] her robe, as we will explain on that [passage]! And one can say: It implied that there was a short time there, similar to [the case of a stain on] flesh, and it answers that it was from a distant time, and [one could] say: She sensed, but was not mindful of it. Alternatively, since the majority of her days are impure, there is reason to be concerned.

Tosafot on Niddah 57b:22:1.hebrew: על בשרה ודאי מגופה אתאי - וא"ת: מאי שנא דלקמן בשמעתין, גבי לבשה שלשה חלוקות ועברה בשוק של טבחים, תולה אפילו בתחתון, ולא אמרינן: אי איתא דמעלמא אתאי, אעליון ה"ל לאשתכוחי? ויש לומר: דהתם, לפעמים שהיא מגלה חלוקה העליון ואתי על התחתון; אבל אי דרך לגלות בשרה:
Tosafot on Niddah 57b:22:1.english: On her flesh, it certainly came from her body - And if you say: What is the difference, that later in our sugya, regarding [a woman who] wore three robes and passed through the marketplace of butchers, she attributes [the stain] even on the innermost [robe], and we do not say: "If it were so that it came from the outside world, it should have been found on the outermost [robe]"? And one can say: There, sometimes she uncovers her outer robe and [the blood] comes onto the inner [robe]; but it is not the way [for her] to uncover her flesh.

Tosafot on Niddah 57b:23:1.hebrew: קתני מיהא על בשרה כו' - וא"ת, ומאי קושיא? ה"נ אימור ארגשה ולאו אדעתה, כדאמר לעיל. וי"ל, דהתם, דרוב ימיה טמאין, יש רגלים לדבר שיש לתלות בהרגשה ולאו אדעתה; אבל הכא, אין שום הוכחה שנתלה בהרגשה ולאו אדעתה, שאין רק שעה מועטת שהוא על בשרה:
Tosafot on Niddah 57b:23:1.english: In any event, it teaches: [If blood is found] on her flesh, etc. - And if you say: And what is the difficulty? Here too, say that she sensed [the blood], but it was not on her mind, as [the Gemara] said above. And one can say that there, where most of her days she is impure, there is a basis to attribute [the blood] to a sensation of which she was unaware; but here, there is no proof [whatsoever] for us to attribute [it] to a sensation of which she was unaware, as [the stain] has been on her flesh for only a short time.

Tosafot on Niddah 57b:23:2.hebrew: מודה שמואל שהיא טמאה מדרבנן - פי' הקונטרס דתלינן דלמא ארגשה ולאו אדעתה. ואין נראה, דאפילו מוחזק לה שלא הרגישה, טמאה, הואיל וראתה דם נדות. ורב אשי נמי מודה דלשמואל היכא דלא הרגישה טהורה מן התורה וטמאה מדרבנן; אלא אתי לפרושי דכי נמצא אקרקע, דטהורה אפילו מדרבנן:
Tosafot on Niddah 57b:23:2.english: Shmuel concedes that she is impure by Rabbinic law - Rashi explained that we assume that perhaps she sensed [an emission] but was not mindful of it. And this does not appear [correct], for even if it is established regarding her that she did not sense, she is [rabbinically] impure, since she saw menstrual blood. And Rav Ashi also concedes that according to Shmuel, where she did not sense, she is pure by Torah law and impure by Rabbinic law; rather, [Rav Ashi] comes to explain that when [blood] is found on the ground, she is pure even by Rabbinic law.
